issues.body: The new rustdoc says each backend's output was verified with an "independent strict single-member decoder," but the relevant test helper uses `flate2::read::GzDecoder`. As the new text itself notes for flate2's CRC implementation, flate2 selects its implementation from the active backend features; the decoder therefore uses zlib-rs when testing zlib-rs and zlib-ng when testing zlib-ng. Single-member strictness is useful, but it does not make this an implementation-independent interoperability check. This overstates the evidence behind the RFC 1952, flush-boundary, and combined-CRC claims.
issues.fix_hint: Either add a genuinely independent decoder check for artifacts produced separately under each backend (for example, checked fixtures decoded by a different gzip implementation, with feature-specific generation made explicit), or accurately reword the statement to say the output was round-tripped through flate2's strict single-member decoder and avoid claiming independent verification.
issues.title: Validation is incorrectly described as using an independent decoder

verdict.summary: The backend-selection documentation is generally coherent, but it overstates the independence of the validation used to support the format-invariant claim. The existing strict single-member helper decodes through flate2, whose implementation switches with the same feature as the encoder; it is therefore not an independent decoder for either backend.
